comments.body:
**Fixed on main, not pushed: 17cef75b, da642a9d, acf1f47e.** All four were tests assuming macOS or racing; none was a daemon bug. At 1aca4f11, `./dev --linux` passes (aarch64 natively, x86_64 emulated) and so does `./dev`.

- `a_confirmed_send_the_pane_does_not_take_is_refused` and `api_corpus::driving` assumed macOS's canonical-mode limit. Linux delivers a line of up to 4095 bytes whole, so the 1103-byte line reached `cat` intact and DONE was right. Measured in the Linux test container. The pane now turns echo off, reads one line with the shell's `read` and prints its first 600 characters, which shows only a line's start on both platforms. Against a daemon that ignores `confirm`, both still fail. The corpus case's copy in `corpus/api-baseline/` changed with it, because the release copies that file only when it bumps.
- `a_connection_that_never_reads_again_is_hung_up_on_without_its_farewell` was a test race, not socket buffers: a Linux socket pair takes about 214 KB before a write blocks, far under the 4 MiB frames. When the writer thread started after the queue had filled, it found the socket empty and rightly wrote the farewell. A diagnostic run showed four frames pushed and only `bye 0 0` read. It passed alone and failed every time beside the other 296 unit tests, and the macOS failure at load 14.4 was the same race. The test now waits until the writer holds a frame before filling the queue.
- `ending_the_control_reader_cancels_a_carried_wait_while_the_client_stays_open`: the daemon hangs up with the test's trailing request unread, and Linux reports a Unix socket closed with unread input to its peer as ECONNRESET, where macOS reports the end of the stream. The test now accepts either.

Carded along the way: a_2sCsk8TK6, `--confirm` answering done on a Linux pane for a line over 4095 bytes that arrived cut short.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Four daemon tests fail on Linux every time, on x86_64 and aarch64 alike, and they block the 0.20.0 release. CI's `linux` job (gate.yml) has failed on every main run since `62cae2f5` on 2026-10-28, when the API landed: on `62cae2f5`, `a5cce8c4` and `c44a075a`. The macOS gate stays green, and the `linux` job was green on every run before that. Latest run: https://github.com/amterp/muster/actions/runs/41329125224

- `api_driving::a_confirmed_send_the_pane_does_not_take_is_refused` (crates/muster-daemon/tests/daemon/api_driving.rs:37): a confirmed `pane.send` to a pane that never takes the text is answered DONE, where REFUSED is expected (`left: (Done, Unspecified)`, `right: (Refused, Unspecified)`).
- `api_corpus::driving`: the same behavior as a recorded case in `corpus/conformance/api-driving.json`, "a confirmed send is done once the pane shows it, and refused when the pane never takes it".
- `control::tests::a_connection_that_never_reads_again_is_hung_up_on_without_its_farewell` (crates/muster-daemon/src/control.rs:812): "the farewell was written to a client that was not reading". On macOS it failed once in CI at a load of 14.4 against 3 performance cores, and passed on a rerun and in local gates. On Linux it fails every time. One unchecked guess: Linux Unix-socket buffers are large enough that the test's 4 MiB frames do not hold the writer, so the writer never blocks and the farewell gets through. Whether a CPU-starved writer on macOS can produce the same outcome is open.
- `linked::ending_the_control_reader_cancels_a_carried_wait_while_the_client_stays_open` (crates/muster-daemon/tests/daemon/linked.rs:200): unwrap on `Err("Connection reset by peer (os error 104)")`.

`./dev --linux` runs these suites locally.

Release state while this is open: `c44a075a chore: 0.20.0` is pushed to main, with the cask naming 0.20.0, still carrying 0.19.0's checksum and its "release under way" marker. Nothing is tagged, there is no GitHub release, and the tap's cask is untouched. Once main's `linux` job is green, `qm run -- ./release minor` resumes the release and tags HEAD at that point.
title: Four daemon tests fail on Linux since the API landed, blocking 0.20.0
